title: Signal cross-references in description and proposed_resolution must use full UUIDs, not short hashes or partial IDs
description: Signal a1000064-0606-4000-8000-000000000064 references other signals using a short hash ('6bfc810c') and apparent partial IDs ('a1000031', 'a7f3e2b1', 'b8f4e3c2') in its description and proposed_resolution fields. These do not resolve to catalogue files and cannot be followed by tooling or agents. The canonical identity of every signal is its full UUID4 (e.g. 'a1000064-0606-4000-8000-000000000064'). Cross-referencing by anything shorter breaks dedup lookup and any future tooling that traverses signal links.
proposed_resolution:
1. Add an authoring rule to the QA Architect persona and skill documentation: when referencing another signal, always use its full signal_id UUID (8-4-4-4-12 hex); never use short hashes or partial IDs.
2. Add a validation step to the Canonical Signal Dedup-and-Write Procedure that scans description and proposed_resolution for UUID-shaped tokens and warns when a non-UUID signal reference pattern is detected.
3. Backfill a1000064-0606-4000-8000-000000000064 to replace short-hash references with either the correct full UUID or a prose-only description if the referenced signal no longer exists in the catalogue.
